Low-chill apples: HRMN-99, Anna and Dorsett Golden

By Gafar Laiya, Gujarat Bio Organics · Updated 2026-11-25

HRMN-99 (promoted by the National Innovation Foundation), Anna and Dorsett Golden are low-chill apples needing only 250–500 hours below 7°C, so they fruit in warm valleys at 400–1,400 m where Delicious cannot. They ripen early, in June, but keep only 10–12 days.

HRMN-99, Anna (low chill)
Tree habit and fruitLow-chill
Chilling need250–500 hours below 7°C (HRMN-99 300–500); 400–1,400 m and warm valleys
Role in the orchardHRMN-99 is self-fertile; Anna and Dorsett Golden need cross-pollination
StrengthsFruit where standard apples get too little winter cold; early June ripening for fresh local markets.
WeaknessesShort shelf life of 10–12 days; not a storage apple.

HRMN-99 is self-fertile; Anna and Dorsett Golden must be planted together to pollinate each other. Because the fruit keeps only 10–12 days, plan to sell fresh in nearby markets. Before planting in a new area, check how many hours your winter actually spends below 7°C, and ask your state horticulture department or KVK about local trial results.

Rootstock, spacing and feeding

Choose the rootstock by soil, not by variety alone: M.9 only on deep, fertile, irrigated land with a trellis; MM.106 only on well-drained soil; MM.111 on drier slopes (rootstock guide). Feed by tree age with our apple fertilizer calculator.

Pollination

Keep 25–33% compatible pollinizers flowering at the same time, 4–6 beehives per hectare at bloom, a boron spray at pink bud, and no sprays during full bloom.

Compare: all apple varieties and rootstocks.

Questions farmers ask

How much chilling does HRMN-99, Anna (low chill) need?

250–500 hours below 7°C (HRMN-99 300–500); 400–1,400 m and warm valleys.

Does HRMN-99, Anna (low chill) need a pollinizer?

HRMN-99 is self-fertile; Anna and Dorsett Golden need cross-pollination.

What are the problems with HRMN-99, Anna (low chill)?

Short shelf life of 10–12 days; not a storage apple.
